questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The language, because it's related to my studies.
It was close to the sea, and not crowded with tourist from all over the world, which made it easier to speak spanish in stead of english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was all right. But with that said, I don't think I had all the information before arrival, which was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The only assistance I got was the information on the welcome day, at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I used the website called idealista.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Here in Almería almost all Erasmus students lives the area of the town that is called Zapillo. It is close to the university, city center and next to the sea. And most Erasmus events is situated or started in Zapillo. And the campus price is to expensive compared to a room in Zapillo.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think the whole registration process with the university and mobility online was a little confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked with other students, and my home university about it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of trouble with finding 5 courses that would be relevant for my study, and at the same time not overlap in hours.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When picking courses, in addition to interest of the courses have in mind the hours they are scheduled for, so the courses will not overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level in the clases ranged from sufficient to demanding. But I think a lot of them require to much work for only 6 ects points.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I think that I my home university the students are more involved in classes.
At my host university the classes were divided into to parts, one was the lecture class, were most of the times the teachers talked for the whole time. And then there were the group work classes, were the students are doing some kind of assignment.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Análisis Crítico del discurso español.
Literatura Norteamericana: Siglo XIX
Historía de lingüística
Literatura  Española del Siglo de Oro
Literatura Norteamericana: Siglo XIX

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All the courses was very interesting, but it also depends on the students level of spanish. 
Literatura Norteamericana: Siglo XIX and Literatura Norteamericana: Siglo XIX was in english.
the others in spanish, and requires a demanding level of spanish do understand.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some repairs on my bike

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food in grocery stores was a little bit more expensive that I would have thought.
If you go for tapas, in Almería it's really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You could play sports such as volley and Football. We had an Erasmus team in a university competition played over months. That was fun.
There is also a gym. that is cheap but in bad condition. and a Swimming pool for training.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like football, find a team, it's so much fun. I got some really good friends because of that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the beach, it's very lively every day.
Go to Cabo de Gata an hour from Almería, it's really beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it's quite easy, but only if you embrace it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make contact to them, in stead of waiting for them to make contact with you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: their relationship with time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The tapas culture in Almería is different to most places in spain. that is really cool.
The way the local uses the beach, it's really cool.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you have 5 courses, the amount of school is demanding, so remember to take some breaks an enjoy your stay, even if it seems overwhelming.

Go to as much of the social stuff in the beginning and build a social environment, it will make the stay so much better.

Go to bars, it's a really good way to meat locals to speak and practice your spanish.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Andalucian spanish is hard to understand, so practice as much spanish before going here.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of living abroad for 5 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To do all the things that the 5 courses demanded and at the same time socialize as much as you wanted to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
